children: U.S. stocks fell as the 10-year Treasury yield jumped back over 5% to the highest level since 2007.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite paced the day's losses after hitting record highs in the previous two sessions, falling 308.24 points, or 1.13%, to 26936.04. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 352.10 points, or 0.68%, to 51511.59. The S&P 500 fell 58.61 points, or 0.75%, to 7706.03.

Oil futures rose 1.8% to $92.16 a barrel in the U.S., snapping a five-session losing streak. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said at the United Nations that Iran is ready for negotiations to end the conflict with the U.S. but warned that Tehran will never surrender to what he called Washington's bullying, or give up its nuclear program.

The yield on the 10-year Treasury note jumped 0.147 percentage point to 5.113%, marking its highest level since July 2007. The yield on the 30-year bond rose 0.099 percentage point to 5.401%, making its biggest one-day leap since May to reach its highest level since 2004. The yield on the two-year Treasury note climbed 0.118 percentage point to 4.893%, its highest in more than two years.

The bonds selloff comes despite efforts by the Treasury Department to cool down long-term yields by increasing its buying of long-term bonds. The department said Wednesday it will buy back as much as $6 billion in 20-year and 30-year bonds on Thursday.

Fed governor Michael Barr said he expects the central bank would likely need to raise interest rates further to tamp down inflation. Before last week's quarter-point rate hike, "we were out of position, and we made an adjustment in the right direction," Barr said in a speech in Chicago. "In my base case, further policy adjustments are likely to be needed to ensure inflation comes down to target in a timely fashion."
Odds of a rate hike next month rose near 70%, from under 50% a week ago, according to the CME FedWatch tool.
